nodes.name: One-pot liquid-phase synthesis
nodes.procedure: In a typical preparation of quinary Mo₁-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs, Pt(acac)₂ (7.9 mg), Pd(acac)₂ (12.2 mg), Ni(acac)₂ (10.3 mg) and Zn(acac)₂ (10.6 mg) were added into a four-neck flask containing 12 mL of OAm. This mixture was then heated to 80°C in vacuum and maintained for 15 min under magnetic stirring to remove air and water. Afterward, the flask was purged with nitrogen (N₂) and cooled to room temperature. After Mo(CO)₆ (20.0 mg) and AA (30.0 mg) were added into the mixture, the flask was evacuated again for 10 min. Then, the flask was filled with N₂ and heated to 200°C under magnetic stirring. Cu(acac)₂ (7.8 mg) dissolved in 0.5 mL OAm and 0.5 mL toluene was then added dropwise to the above mixture under magnetic stirring. After the injection, the mixed solution was heated at 200°C for 2 h. At last, the reaction mixture was rapidly cooled down to room temperature and collected by centrifugation. Finally, the products were washed two or three times with a cyclohexane/ethanol mixture.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images display Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs dominated by 2D graphene-like ultrathin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Representative transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and low-magnification high-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) images display that the Mo₁-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs are entirely dominated by two-dimensional (2D) graphene-like ultrathin nanosheets (Supplementary Fig. 5 and Fig. 1b).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern exhibits typical fcc structure of Pd (PDF# 46-1043) without apparent phase segregation, with weakening and broadening of diffraction peaks revealing lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern exhibits a typical fcc structure of Pd (PDF# 46-1043) without apparent phase segregation, implying the successful creation of HEAs. Meanwhile, the weakening and broadening of diffraction peaks reveal the presence of lattice distortion.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS determines Pd/Pt/Ni/Cu/Zn/Mo atomic ratio of 24.1/14.6/26.3/22.1/11.1/1.8 in Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs, in agreement with STEM-EDS and ICP-OES.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic ratio of Pd/Pt/Ni/Cu/Zn/Mo in Mo₁-PdPtNi-CuZn SAHEA NSs is determined to be 24.1/14.6/26.3/22.1/11.1/1.8 by inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS), in well agreement with the STEM energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (STEM-EDS) and inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) results.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM determines average thickness of Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs to be about 1.69 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The average thickness was determined by atomic force microscopy (AFM) to be about 1.69 nm, further confirming their ultrathin character.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals polycrystalline properties and abundant atomic-scale concave defects in individual Mo1-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, the polycrystalline properties and abundant atomic-scale concave defects can be revealed by the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image taken from individual Mo₁-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NS.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM reveals high-crystallinity with clear lattice fringes of (111) facets; average lattice spacing varies from 0.233 nm to 0.237 nm indicating ~4.4% intrinsic tensile strain.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM image further reveals the high-crystallinity of Mo₁-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs with the clear lattice fringes of (111) facets... The average lattice spacing varies from 0.233 nm to 0.237 nm, indicating substantial lattice distortions and ~4.4% intrinsic tensile strain.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM-EDS elemental mapping demonstrates homogeneous distribution of Pd, Pt, Ni, Cu, Zn and isolated Mo atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental EDS mapping demonstrates the homogeneous distribution of Pd, Pt, Ni, Cu, and Zn elements, and isolated Mo atoms in the Mo₁-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs (Fig. 1k).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Pd, Pt, Ni, Cu, Zn, Mo; Pd, Pt, Ni, Cu, Zn mainly in metallic states, Mo primarily in oxidation states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) analysis was performed to further confirm the presence of Pd, Pt, Ni, Cu, Zn, and Mo... Note that Pd, Pt, Ni, Cu, and Zn atoms are mainly in the metallic states, while Mo atoms are primarily in the oxidation states.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution EDX elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Pd, Pt, Ni, Cu, Zn elements and sporadic but even isolated Mo atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution EDX elemental mapping demonstrates that Pd, Pt, Ni, Cu, and Zn elements are uniformly distributed throughout the Mo₁·PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs. However, Mo atoms are distributed sporadically but evenly doped into the NSs in the form of an isolated atom.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic-level EELS line-scanning confirms Mo atoms exist as single atoms with signature M4,5 edge.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic-level electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) line-scanning acquisition was further performed to confirm that Mo atoms existed as single atoms... The spectra demonstrate the presence of a Mo atom in these atomic columns.

nodes.characterization_summary: Mo K-edge XANES shows higher adsorption threshold and white line intensity than Mo foil indicating high valence states; FT-EXAFS shows major Mo-O peak at ~1.33 Å with absent Mo-Mo scattering confirming atomically dispersed Mo sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra show that the Mo K-edge adsorption threshold position and white line intensity of Mo₁-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs are higher than those of Mo foil... The k³-weight FT-EXAFS spectra reveal that the Mo₁-PdPtNiCuZn SAHEA NSs exhibit the major peak at ~1.33 Å, attributed to Mo-O scattering... The characteristic peak of Mo-Mo scattering (~2.34 Å for the Mo foil) is almost absent.
